lead: About 510 soldiers are heading to Durban to back police after violent anti-immigration protests, as KZN braces for severe storms and the country enters the final week before the 4 November local elections.

items.title: Ramaphosa sends 510 soldiers to KZN after violent Durban protests
items.summary: The SANDF deployment will support police in Durban until 30 November under Operation Prosper, at a cost of about R34 million, following anti-immigration marches that turned violent in the CBD.

items.title: Severe storms and flooding warning for KwaZulu-Natal today
items.summary: The Weather Service has yellow warnings for eastern and western KZN, with heavy rain, hail and damaging winds that could flood roads and low-lying areas. The Eastern Cape coast also faces disruptive rain.

items.title: Final week of campaigning before 4 November local elections
items.summary: Special votes take place on 2 and 3 November, and polls open 7am to 9pm on election day. Metro voters get two ballots, other municipalities three; only an SA ID or temporary ID certificate is accepted.

items.title: Poll puts MK well ahead in eThekwini as Ramaphosa brushes off surveys
items.summary: An eNCA-MarkData poll has MK on 48% in eThekwini, the DA on 25% and the ANC on 14.5%. Ramaphosa, campaigning in Mamelodi, said the ANC is heading for outright wins regardless of polling.

items.title: Water restrictions across large parts of eThekwini
items.summary: The city limited supply from the Durban Heights works after heavy demand drained reservoirs, affecting areas including Pinetown South, Folweni and KwaSanti. Residents are asked to use water sparingly; no end date was given.

items.title: Zuma-Sambudla trial: police found no money trail to July 2021 unrest
items.summary: A detective told the Durban High Court that bank and phone records showed no financial links between the former MK MP and groups behind the unrest. Her incitement trial continues today.

items.title: Bronkhorstspruit stomach-illness cases climb past 800
items.summary: Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina said 833 people have now fallen ill in the outbreak linked to contaminated municipal water east of Pretoria.

items.title: Eugene de Kock testifies at inquiry into stalled apartheid-era prosecutions
items.summary: The former Vlakplaas commander told the commission he was never asked to give evidence against senior politicians and generals, and questioned why he alone was prosecuted.

items.title: Lula wins fourth term in Brazil; Trump calls vote 'rigged' without evidence
items.summary: Lula da Silva beat Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's runoff. Bolsonaro initially rejected the result and says he will now lead the opposition; Trump questioned the outcome without offering proof.

items.title: Serbia's student-led list wins parliament as Vučić concedes
items.summary: Preliminary projections give the Student List roughly 135-140 of 250 seats in the snap election, a majority, ending the long dominance of Aleksandar Vučić's SNS.

items.title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after deadly church attack
items.summary: Following Friday's gun attack on a church funeral in Karak that killed at least nine, Jordan's military hit targets in Syria's Daraa and Suwayda provinces and arrested three suspects.

items.title: Mass arrests at French cost-of-living and schools protests
items.summary: Police detained more than 1,300 people during weekend demonstrations, with organisers estimating 250,000 marched in Paris despite a decree limiting protests.

items.title: Israeli demolitions in Hebron days before Israel's election
items.summary: After an attack killed two soldiers at a checkpoint, Israeli forces razed or marked buildings across part of Hebron, displacing about 1,500 people, with Israel's national vote days away.

items.title: Algeria orders troops into neighbouring Niger
items.summary: Algeria's president ordered a deployment to Niger after the upper house of parliament approved it at the weekend.

items.title: Rand slips towards R16.64 to the dollar
items.summary: The rand weakened about 0.3% on Monday and is down roughly 1.4% over the past month, pressured by high oil prices and softer metals after briefly touching R16.40 around the mid-term budget.

items.title: Another big fuel hike looms for November
items.summary: Mid-month Central Energy Fund data pointed to petrol rising about R1.84-R1.88 a litre and diesel about R1.25-R1.29, with Brent near $115 driving the increase. The official adjustment is due on 4 November.

items.title: Busy data week: PPI on Thursday, trade figures Friday
items.summary: Stats SA releases September producer inflation on Thursday alongside credit data, followed by budget and trade balance numbers on Friday. Treasury briefs on Operation Vulindlela the same day.

items.title: Proteas and Australia start Newlands decider level at 1-1
items.summary: The third Test begins today in Cape Town. Gerald Coetzee replaces the injured Anrich Nortje in an otherwise unchanged Proteas side after the innings win in Gqeberha.

items.title: Sundowns and Chiefs out of Africa; Pirates and Durban City advance
items.summary: Holders Sundowns fell to Angola's Wiliete on away goals and Chiefs lost on penalties to Red Arrows. Pirates beat African Stars 5-0 on aggregate and Durban City won 6-1 to reach the group stages.

items.title: Arsenal level with Man City at the top of the Premier League
items.summary: Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 while City lost 2-1 at Aston Villa, leaving both on 21 points; Tottenham won 2-0 at Chelsea.

items.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 staff
items.summary: The time-limited exit offer covers employees on selected teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK, following around 4,800 job cuts in July.
